# precmed

## Overview

**precmed** was developed to help researchers with the implementation of
precision medicine in R. A key objective of precision medicine is to
determine the optimal treatment separately for each patient instead of
applying a common treatment to all patients. Personalizing treatment
decisions becomes particularly relevant when treatment response differs
across patients, or when patients have different preferences about
benefits and harms. This package offers statistical methods to develop
and validate prediction models for estimating individualized treatment
effects. These treatment effects are also known as the conditional
average treatment effects (CATEs) and describe how different subgroups
of patients respond to the same treatment. Presently, **precmed**
focuses on the personalization of two competitive treatments using
randomized data from a clinical trial (Zhao et al. 2013) or using
real-world data (RWD) from a non-randomized study (Yadlowsky et al.
2020).

For guidance on visualizing and interpreting individualized treatment
rules, see Chapter 20, “Visualization and interpretation of
individualized treatment rule results”, by Jiang et al. in *Comparative
Effectiveness and Personalized Medicine Research Using Real-World Data*
(Jiang et al. 2026). The [companion
tutorial](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/comparative-effectiveness/chapter_18.html)
includes examples using **precmed**.

## Installation

The `precmed` package can be installed from CRAN as follows:

``` r

install.packages("precmed")
```

The latest version can be installed from GitHub as follows:

``` r

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github(repo = "smartdata-analysis-and-statistics/precmed")
```

## Package capabilities

The main functions in the **precmed** package are:

| Function | Description |
|----|----|
| [catefit](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefit.html)() | Estimation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) |
| [atefit](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/atefit.html)() | Doubly robust estimator for the average treatment effect (ATE) |
| [catecv](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecv.html)() | Development and cross-validation of the CATE |
| [abc](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/abc.html)() | Compute the area between the average treatment difference curve of competing models for the CATE (Zhao et al. 2013) |
| [plot](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/plot.precmed.html)() | Two side-by-side line plots of validation curves from the `precmed` object |
| [boxplot](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/boxplot.precmed.html)() | Plot the proportion of subjects with an estimated treatment effect no less than $`c`$ over a range of values for $`c`$ (Zhao et al. 2013). |

For more info:
<https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/>

## Recommended workflow

We recommend the following workflow to develop a model for estimating
the CATE in order to identify treatment effect heterogeneity:

1.  Compare up to five modelling approaches (e.g., Poisson regression,
    boosting) for estimating the CATE using cross-validation through
    [catecv](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecv.html).
2.  Select the best modelling approach using 3 metrics:
    - Compare the steepness of the validation curves in the validation
      samples across methods using
      [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html). Two
      side-by-side plots are generated, visualizing the estimated
      average treatment effects in a series of nested subgroups. On the
      left side the curve is shown for the training set, and on the
      right side the curve is shown for the validation set. Each line in
      the plots represents one scoring method (e.g., boosting,
      randomForest) specified under the argument `score.method`.
    - The area between curves (ABC) using
      [abc](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/abc.html)
      quantifies a model’s ability to capture treatment effect
      heterogeneity. Higher ABC values are preferable as they indicate
      that more treatment effect heterogeneity is captured by the
      scoring method.
    - Compare the distribution of the estimated ATE across different
      levels of the CATE score percentiles using
      [`boxplot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/boxplot.html).
3.  Apply the best modelling approach in the original data or in a new
    external dataset using
    [`catefit()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefit.md).
4.  Optional. Use
    [`atefit()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/atefit.md)
    to estimate ATE between 2 treatment groups with a doubly robust
    estimator and estimate the variability of the ATE with a bootstrap
    approach.

In the vignettes, we will adopt a different workflow to gradually expose
the user from simple to more complex methods.

## User input

When applying
[`catefit()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefit.md)
or
[`catecv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecv.md),
the user has to (at least) input:

- `response`: type of outcome/response (either `count` or `survival`)  
- `data`: a data frame with individual patient data  
- `score.method`: methods to estimate the CATE (e.g., `boosting`,
  `poisson`, `twoReg`, `contrastReg`)  
- `cate.model`: a formula describing the outcome model (e.g., outcome ~
  age + gender + previous_treatment)  
- `ps.model`: a formula describing the propensity score model to adjust
  for confounding (e.g., treatment ~ age + previous_treatment)

# References

Jiang, Xiaotong, Gabrielle Simoneau, Fabio Pellegrini, Changyu Shen,
Carl de Moor, and Lu Tian. 2026. “Visualization and Interpretation of
Individualized Treatment Rule Results.” In *Comparative Effectiveness
and Personalized Medicine Research Using Real-World Data*, edited by
Thomas P. A. Debray, Tri-Long Nguyen, and Robert W. Platt, 513–36.
Chapman & Hall/CRC.
<https://www.routledge.com/Comparative-Effectiveness-and-Personalized-Medicine-Research-Using-Rea/Debray-Nguyen-Platt/p/book/9781032292748>.

Yadlowsky, Steve, Fabio Pellegrini, Federica Lionetto, Stefan Braune,
and Lu Tian. 2020. “Estimation and Validation of Ratio-Based Conditional
Average Treatment Effects Using Observational Data.” *Journal of the
American Statistical Association*, 1–18.

Zhao, Lihui, Lu Tian, Tianxi Cai, Brian Claggett, and Lee-Jen Wei. 2013.
“Effectively Selecting a Target Population for a Future Comparative
Study.” *Journal of the American Statistical Association* 108 (502):
527–39. <https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2013.770705>.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`abc()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/abc.md)
  :

  Compute the area between curves from the `"precmed"` object

- [`abc(`*`<precmed>`*`)`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/abc.precmed.md)
  :

  Compute the area between curves from the `"precmed"` object

- [`arg.checks()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/arg.checks.md)
  :

  Check arguments Catered to all types of outcome Apply at the beginning
  of `pmcount()`, `cvcount()`, `drcount.inference()`,
  [`catefitsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefitsurv.md),
  [`catecvsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecvsurv.md),
  and `drsurv.inference()`

- [`arg.checks.common()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/arg.checks.common.md)
  :

  Check arguments that are common to all types of outcome USed inside
  [`arg.checks()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/arg.checks.md)

- [`atefit()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/atefit.md)
  : Doubly robust estimator of and inference for the average treatment
  effect for count, survival and continuous data

- [`atefitcount()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/atefitcount.md)
  : Doubly robust estimator of and inference for the average treatment
  effect for count data

- [`atefitmean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/atefitmean.md)
  : Doubly robust estimator of and inference for the average treatment
  effect for continuous data

- [`atefitsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/atefitsurv.md)
  : Doubly robust estimator of and inference for the average treatment
  effect for survival data

- [`auc()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/auc.md)
  : Compute the area under the curve using linear or natural spline
  interpolation

- [`balance.split()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/balance.split.md)
  : Split the given dataset into balanced training and validation sets
  (within a pre-specified tolerance) Balanced means 1) The ratio of
  treated and controls is maintained in the training and validation
  sets 2) The covariate distributions are balanced between the training
  and validation sets

- [`balancemean.split()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/balancemean.split.md)
  : Split the given dataset into balanced training and validation sets
  (within a pre-specified tolerance) Balanced means 1) The ratio of
  treated and controls is maintained in the training and validation
  sets 2) The covariate distributions are balanced between the training
  and validation sets

- [`balancesurv.split()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/balancesurv.split.md)
  : Split the given time-to-event dataset into balanced training and
  validation sets (within a pre-specified tolerance) Balanced means 1)
  The ratio of treated and controls is maintained in the training and
  validation sets 2) The covariate distributions are balanced between
  the training and validation sets

- [`boxplot(`*`<precmed>`*`)`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/boxplot.precmed.md)
  :

  A set of box plots of estimated ATEs from the `"precmed"` object

- [`catecv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecv.md)
  : Cross-validation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE)
  score for count, survival or continuous outcomes

- [`catecvcount()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecvcount.md)
  : Cross-validation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE)
  score for count outcomes

- [`catecvmean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecvmean.md)
  : Cross-validation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE)
  score for continuous outcomes

- [`catecvsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecvsurv.md)
  : Cross-validation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE)
  score for survival outcomes

- [`catefit()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefit.md)
  : Estimation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) score
  for count, survival and continuous data

- [`catefitcount()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefitcount.md)
  : Estimation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) score
  for count data

- [`catefitmean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefitmean.md)
  : Estimation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) score
  for continuous data

- [`catefitsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefitsurv.md)
  : Estimation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) score
  for survival data

- [`countExample`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/countExample.md)
  : Simulated data with count outcome

- [`cox.rmst()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/cox.rmst.md)
  : Estimate restricted mean survival time (RMST) based on Cox
  regression model

- [`data.preproc()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/data.preproc.md)
  :

  Data preprocessing Apply at the beginning of `pmcount()` and
  `cvcount()`, after
  [`arg.checks()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/arg.checks.md)

- [`data.preproc.mean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/data.preproc.mean.md)
  :

  Data preprocessing Apply at the beginning of
  [`catefitmean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefitmean.md)
  and
  [`catecvmean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecvmean.md),
  after
  [`arg.checks()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/arg.checks.md)

- [`data.preproc.surv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/data.preproc.surv.md)
  :

  Data preprocessing Apply at the beginning of
  [`catefitcount()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefitcount.md),
  [`catecvcount()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecvcount.md),
  [`catefitsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catefitsurv.md),
  and
  [`catecvsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/catecvsurv.md),
  after
  [`arg.checks()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/arg.checks.md)

- [`drcount()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/drcount.md)
  : Doubly robust estimator of the average treatment effect for count
  data

- [`drmean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/drmean.md)
  : Doubly robust estimator of the average treatment effect for
  continuous data

- [`drsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/drsurv.md)
  : Doubly robust estimator of the average treatment effect with Cox
  model for survival data

- [`estcount.bilevel.subgroups()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/estcount.bilevel.subgroups.md)
  : Estimate the Average Treatment Effect of the log risk ratio in
  multiple bi-level subgroups defined by the proportions

- [`estcount.multilevel.subgroup()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/estcount.multilevel.subgroup.md)
  : Estimate the ATE of the log RR ratio in one multilevel subgroup
  defined by the proportions

- [`estmean.bilevel.subgroups()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/estmean.bilevel.subgroups.md)
  : Estimate the ATE of the mean difference in multiple bi-level
  subgroups defined by the proportions

- [`estmean.multilevel.subgroup()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/estmean.multilevel.subgroup.md)
  : Estimate the ATE of the mean difference in one multilevel subgroup
  defined by the proportions

- [`estsurv.bilevel.subgroups()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/estsurv.bilevel.subgroups.md)
  : Estimate the ATE of the RMTL ratio and unadjusted hazard ratio in
  multiple bi-level subgroups defined by the proportions

- [`estsurv.multilevel.subgroups()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/estsurv.multilevel.subgroups.md)
  : Estimate the ATE of the RMTL ratio and unadjusted hazard ratio in
  one multilevel subgroup defined by the proportions

- [`generate_kfold_indices()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/generate_kfold_indices.md)
  : Generate K-fold Indices for Cross-Validation

- [`glm.ps()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/glm.ps.md)
  : Propensity score estimation with LASSO

- [`glm.simplereg.ps()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/glm.simplereg.ps.md)
  : Propensity score estimation with a linear model

- [`intxcount()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/intxcount.md)
  : Estimate the CATE model using specified scoring methods

- [`intxmean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/intxmean.md)
  : Estimate the CATE model using specified scoring methods

- [`intxsurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/intxsurv.md)
  : Estimate the CATE model using specified scoring methods for survival
  outcomes

- [`ipcw.surv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/ipcw.surv.md)
  : Probability of being censored

- [`meanCatch()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/meanCatch.md)
  : Catch errors and warnings when estimating the ATEs in the nested
  subgroup for continuous data

- [`meanExample`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/meanExample.md)
  : Simulated data with a continuous outcome

- [`onearmglmcount.dr()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/onearmglmcount.dr.md)
  : Doubly robust estimators of the coefficients in the two regression

- [`onearmglmmean.dr()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/onearmglmmean.dr.md)
  : Doubly robust estimators of the coefficients in the two regression

- [`onearmsurv.dr()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/onearmsurv.dr.md)
  : Doubly robust estimators of the coefficients in the two regression

- [`plot(`*`<atefit>`*`)`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/plot.atefit.md)
  : Histogram of bootstrap estimates

- [`plot(`*`<precmed>`*`)`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/plot.precmed.md)
  :

  Two side-by-side line plots of validation curves from the `"precmed"`
  object

- [`print(`*`<atefit>`*`)`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/print.atefit.md)
  : Print function for atefit

- [`print(`*`<catefit>`*`)`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/print.catefit.md)
  : Print function for atefit

- [`scorecount()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/scorecount.md)
  : Calculate the log CATE score given the baseline covariates and
  follow-up time for specified scoring method methods

- [`scoremean()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/scoremean.md)
  : Calculate the CATE score given the baseline covariates for specified
  scoring method methods

- [`scoresurv()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/scoresurv.md)
  : Calculate the log CATE score given the baseline covariates and
  follow-up time for specified scoring method methods for survival
  outcomes

- [`survCatch()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/survCatch.md)
  : Catch errors and warnings when estimating the ATEs in the nested
  subgroup

- [`survivalExample`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/survivalExample.md)
  : Simulated data with survival outcome

- [`twoarmglmcount.dr()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/twoarmglmcount.dr.md)
  : Doubly robust estimators of the coefficients in the contrast

- [`twoarmglmmean.dr()`](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/precmed/reference/twoarmglmmean.dr.md)
  : Doubly robust estimators of the coefficients in the contrast

  : Doubly robust estimators of the coefficients in the contrast
